topology_reasoning.visual_description: B&W image shows a large oval/racetrack-like closed loop (outer boundary) enclosing two symmetric rectangular 'pad' features (one in the upper-middle, one in the lower-middle), each pad internally divided by a thin bar into two cells, each cell containing a smaller inset window. Each pad connects outward (left and right) via thicker straight/flared arms that reach toward the loop's left and right tips, where the arms and the loop appear to merge into solid material near the very ends of the device.
topology_reasoning.calibration_note: footprint.json declares footprint_um=[3.0, 5.5] with length(x)=3.0um mapped to the image's horizontal bbox (1551px) and width(y)=5.5um mapped to the vertical bbox (780px), giving highly anisotropic pixel scale (sx=517 px/um, sy=141.8 px/um, ratio ~3.65x). The device is REAL-SPACE PORTRAIT (taller than wide, 3.0 x 5.5um) even though the extracted image renders LANDSCAPE (wide oval): the anisotropic calibration stretches a portrait real device horizontally into the observed landscape raster. Column scans of the outer boundary show smooth, continuous curvature (no genuinely flat run), which pointed away from a straight-rail stadium/racetrack (also geometrically infeasible in this footprint: 2*R needed for the observed height would exceed the total width) and toward a pure ellipse/superellipse outer boundary.
topology_reasoning.device_identity: Modeled as an elliptical ring loop with two symmetric internal loading/coupling pads (each a rectangular frame with two window cutouts separated by a divider bar), connected to the loop via tapered arms -- a dual symmetric coupling or phase-shifter-pad structure loaded onto a ring cavity.
function_defining_knobs: ring_ax / ring_ay - ring ellipse centerline semi-axes (resonator size / FSR)
ring_n - superellipse exponent (2=ellipse; left at 2.0, an n=4 superellipse trial hurt IoU)
ring_width - waveguide/rail width of the ring loop
pad_width / pad_height - size of each loading/coupling pad
pad_border - solid frame thickness around each pad's window cutouts
window_width / window_height - size of the two cutout windows inside each pad
divider_width - width of the central bar separating the two windows
pad_offset_y - vertical distance of each pad's center from device center
arm_width - width of the straight arm feeding each pad
arm_flare_width / arm_length - taper geometry connecting pad to ring wall

iterations.change_made: Initial parametric build: elliptical ring (ax=1.15, ay=2.45, width=0.55) + two symmetric pads (0.89x1.04, border 0.25, windows 0.33x0.54, divider 0.11) + tapered arms (0.44->0.90, length 0.95), parameters seeded from direct pixel-measurement / calibration conversion.

Diff showed ring: red inside/blue outside (mine too thick and too small) -> increased ring_ax 1.15->1.25, ring_ay 2.45->2.60, decreased ring_width 0.55->0.42. Pads showed thin red/blue outline (mine slightly small) -> pad_width 0.89->0.95, pad_height 1.04->1.12. Arm flare widened 0.90->1.00, arm_length 0.95->0.85.

Same red-inside/blue-outside ring pattern persisted (weaker) -> ring_ax 1.25->1.35, ring_ay 2.60->2.70, ring_width 0.42->0.34. Pads still slightly small -> pad_width 0.95->1.00, pad_height 1.12->1.17, window_width 0.33->0.30. BEST RESULT.

Diff showed poles (top/bottom) too full and sides too thin for a pure ellipse -> tried superellipse exponent ring_n=4.0 with ring_width reduced to 0.28. Result WORSE (IoU dropped 0.556->0.468) -- superellipse hypothesis rejected.

Reverted ring_n to 2.0 (true ellipse) but kept ring_width=0.28 from iter4. Still below iter-3 best (0.556) -- the width reduction alone (without the superellipse) was also a regression vs iter 3's width=0.34.

Restored ring_n=2.0, ring_width=0.34 (iter-3 ring values). Tried enlarging pads further (pad_width 1.00->1.05, pad_height 1.17->1.22, window_width 0.30->0.35) and arm (flare 1.00->1.10, length 0.85->0.75) to chase residual window/arm diff. Result 0.542, still below iter-3's 0.556 -- reverted to iter-3 parameters as the final, honest best across all 6 iterations.

final.params_used: iteration 3 configuration (see device.py): ring_ax=1.35, ring_ay=2.70, ring_n=2.0, ring_width=0.34, pad_width=1.00, pad_height=1.17, pad_border=0.22, window_width=0.30, window_height=0.54, divider_width=0.11, pad_offset_y=0.91, arm_width=0.44, arm_flare_width=1.00, arm_length=0.85
final.note: 6-iteration budget exhausted below the 0.85 IoU target. The residual gap is dominated by the outer ring boundary shape: the target's outer curve is flatter at the poles and fuller at the sides than a true ellipse (an n=4 superellipse trial made it worse, not better, so the exact curve family was not found within budget). This is an honest partial result, not tuned/fudged to pass.

knob_verification.tool_note: homi.spec_optimization.verify_knob_response is hard-wired to the MZI two-arm lengths.json contract (exactly 2 named arms) from the optimize-to-spec skill; this ring+pad device is not an MZI and does not produce that file, so the literal tool call raises RuntimeError by design (not a bug in this device).
knob_verification.manual_equivalent_check: Perturbed pad_width from 1.00um to 1.30um (delta=0.30um), rebuilt the GDS in isolation, and measured layer-(1,0) polygon area via gdstk.Polygon.area(). Base area=13.6447um^2, perturbed area=14.3467um^2, delta=0.7020um^2. Expected growth = 2 pads * pad_height * delta_width = 2*1.17*0.30 = 0.702um^2 -- exact match. Confirms pad_width drives real, correctly-scaled geometry change, not a cosmetic/report-only knob.
